Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Apex MedTech Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are David Thompson, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; Dr. Lisa Patel, Chief Technology Officer; and Mark Johnson, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to David Thompson.

David Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Apex MedTech had a productive Q3, marked by significant advancements in our product portfolio and expansion into new markets.

Today, I will cover six key aspects of our performance:
1. Overall performance highlights and key achievements
2. SG&A expense management and efficiency gains
3. Competitive dynamics and market share trends
4. Procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary
5. Strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter
6. Revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter/year

Sarah will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. Dr. Patel will follow with updates on our R&D initiatives, and then we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with overall performance highlights and key achievements.

I'm pleased to kick off our Q3 2024 earnings discussion with a strong set of overall performance highlights that underscore our execution across the Medical Devices portfolio amid a resilient yet dynamic market environment.

Starting with the top line, we delivered global revenue of $2.85 billion for the quarter, representing 14% reported growth and 11% organic growth year-over-year. This marks our eighth consecutive quarter of double-digit organic growth, outpacing the broader MedTech industry average of 7-8% as reported by Evaluate MedTech. On an adjusted basis, our diluted EPS came in at $1.92, up 22% from the prior year, driven by robust procedural volumes, modest average selling price expansion of 2%, and disciplined operating leverage. Our adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 210 basis points to 28.5%, reflecting the benefits of our MedTech 2.0 efficiency program, which has now delivered over $450 million in annualized run-rate savings since inception in 2022.

Diving into segment performance, our Cardiovascular franchise led the way with $1.12 billion in revenue, up 16% organically. Structural heart procedures surged 24%, fueled by the continued ramp of our next-generation Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement system, EvoFlow Pro, which captured 18% U.S. market share in its first full quarter post-FDA approval—gaining ground on frontrunners like Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien and Medtronic's CoreValve. Coronary intervention grew 12%, with our bioresorbable scaffold, AbsorbX, achieving 35% procedural adoption in high-volume cath labs, ahead of our internal targets. Electrophysiology rounded out the segment with 14% growth, bolstered by AI-enhanced mapping software integrations that reduced procedure times by an average of 18%.

Our Orthopedics and Spine segment posted $785 million, up 10% organically, resilient despite softer elective volumes in certain U.S. regions impacted by staffing shortages. Key here was the robotic-assisted knee system, RoboKnee 3.0, which drove 28% growth in enabling technologies, mirroring Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci momentum but tailored for orthopedics. Spine revenue grew 13%, with our expandable interbody devices gaining traction in minimally invasive fusions, helping us expand share versus DePuy Synthes.

Surgical Care and Diagnostics delivered $945 million, up 9% organically, with standout performance in endoscopy up 15% thanks to single-use endoscopes addressing post-COVID infection control priorities. Our AI-powered imaging platform, VisionAI, secured CE Mark and early U.S. 510(k) clearance, enabling real-time polyp detection with 95% sensitivity—positioning us competitively against Olympus and Fujifilm in the growing computer vision segment, projected to reach $15 billion by 2028 per Grand View Research.

Regionally, we saw balanced strength. U.S. revenue grew 12% organically to $1.65 billion, supported by favorable reimbursement dynamics under the CY2025 IPPS final rule, which preserved pass-through status for several high-acuity devices. Europe ex-UK climbed 13% on a constant currency basis to $680 million, driven by strong TAVR penetration in Germany and Italy amid aging demographics and HTA approvals. APAC was the star at 22% organic growth to $360 million, led by China ramping to 25% growth post-NMPA approval for EvoFlow Pro, capitalizing on the region's 1.4 billion population and rising PCI volumes. Emerging markets, including Latin America, Middle East, and Africa, contributed 15% growth, with our affordable orthopedics portfolio resonating in cost-sensitive markets.

Key achievements this quarter solidify our leadership trajectory. First, we achieved FDA Breakthrough Device Designation for our fully implantable left ventricular assist device, HeartBridge, accelerating our path to approval in advanced heart failure—a $4 billion addressable market dominated by Abbott's HeartMate. Second, we closed the $1.2 billion acquisition of NeuroVasc Solutions, adding neuromodulation assets that enhance our hypertension therapy pipeline, with Phase III data expected H2 2025. Third, strategic partnerships advanced: a multi-year GPO agreement with Vizient for exclusive supply of our robotic orthopedics suite, securing 15% market access uplift, and a co-development pact with Siemens Healthineers on hybrid OR imaging, targeting the $10 billion robotics market growing at 18% CAGR.

On the innovation front, our R&D investment hit $420 million, or 14.7% of revenue, fueling a pipeline of 12 late-stage programs. We're leaning into megatrends like value-based care, with 40% of our U.S. revenue now tied to bundled payments, and digital health, where our cloud-connected devices achieved 92% uptime and generated $85 million in recurring SaaS revenue—up 45% YoY.

Strategically, these results reflect our focus on high-growth adjacencies, procedural enablement, and margin discipline. We've gained ~150 basis points of global market share YTD, per AlphaSights tracking, while navigating headwinds like raw material inflation mitigated via hedging and supply chain normalization post-semiconductor shortages. Looking ahead, we remain confident in our FY2024 guidance of 11-13% organic growth and 28-29% EBITDA margins, positioning Apex MedTech as the growth engine in a consolidating industry.

Now, let's talk about SG&A expense management and efficiency gains.

As we review our Q3 results, I'm particularly pleased with our disciplined approach to SG&A expense management, which delivered meaningful efficiency gains and supported our adjusted operating margin expansion to 28.2%, up 210 basis points year-over-year. These levers are core to our strategy in the competitive Medical Devices landscape, where peers like Medtronic and Stryker are also prioritizing cost discipline amid moderating procedure volumes and reimbursement pressures.

Starting with the headline numbers: Q3 SG&A came in at $682 million, a 4% increase on a reported basis but only 1% on an organic constant-currency basis, despite 11% organic revenue growth to $2.85 billion. This drove SG&A as a percentage of revenue down 140 basis points to 27.2%—our lowest quarterly level in three years. For the full first nine months, SG&A leverage improved even more dramatically, contracting 220 basis points to 27.5% of sales. This outperforms our peer group average, where companies like Boston Scientific and Abbott Laboratories saw SG&A ratios hover around 29-31% in their recent quarters, per our analysis of consensus data.

To give you a sense of the trends, let's look at the YoY trajectory. In Q3 2023, amid post-COVID supply chain disruptions and elective procedure backlogs, our SG&A ratio peaked at 28.6%, inflated by one-time freight costs and sales force ramp-up for our new TAVR platform, similar to Edwards Lifesciences' experience with Sapien valves. We've since reversed that through a multi-pronged initiative we call "MedTech Lean 2025," targeting $250 million in annualized SG&A savings by year-end, of which we've already realized 60% or $150 million run-rate.

Diving into the components:

Selling Expenses, which are 55% of SG&A, declined 2% YoY to $375 million, or 15.0% of revenue—down from 16.4%. Key driver here was our optimized field sales model. We've reduced our U.S. rep-to-territory ratio from 1:8 to 1:12 by layering in digital enablement tools, including a customized Salesforce Health Cloud integration with AI-powered procedure forecasting. This has boosted sales productivity by 18%, allowing reps to focus on high-value OR conversions for our robotic-assisted systems, akin to Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci ecosystem. We also shifted 25% of customer engagements to virtual peer-to-peer programs, cutting travel by 22% while maintaining win rates above 65% in neurovascular and structural heart.

General & Administrative, 30% of SG&A, was flat YoY at $205 million, but with 5% organic leverage. Our global shared services center in Manila, expanded last year, now handles 70% of AP/AR processing via RPA bots from UiPath, slashing invoice cycle times from 45 to 12 days. Procurement yielded $35 million in savings through strategic sourcing—e.g., consolidating suppliers for biocompatible polymers used in our neuromodulation leads, negotiating 12-15% volume discounts amid stabilizing resin prices post-Ukraine supply shocks.

Corporate & Other, 15% of SG&A, down 8% to $102 million, driven by headcount discipline. We right-sized our global workforce by 4% (net of 2,100 roles), emphasizing attrition over layoffs, and accelerated hybrid work models, reducing facilities costs by 11%. Legal and compliance expenses moderated as FDA 510(k) submissions for our next-gen drug-eluting stents normalized post-IDE trial efficiencies.

Regionally, our efforts shone through varying headwinds. In the U.S., which represents 58% of revenue, SG&A efficiency gained 180 basis points to 26.8%, fueled by value-based care contracts with IDNs like HCA and Kaiser Permanente. These tie reimbursements to outcomes for our orthopedic implants, reducing demo and training costs by 15% via AR/VR simulations. EMEA, at 24% of sales, saw the sharpest improvement—down 250 basis points to 28.5%—despite double-digit inflation and tender delays in Germany for our endoscopy portfolio. We offset this with localized pricing analytics, mirroring Smith & Nephew's playbook in ex-U.S. markets. In high-growth APAC (13% of revenue), SG&A held steady at 29.2% through disciplined distributor incentives, supporting 22% organic growth in China for our electrophysiology catheters amid NMPA approvals.

Strategically, these gains aren't just cost-cutting—they're reinvestment fuel. We're allocating 40% of the $150 million run-rate savings to high-ROI areas: $40 million to commercial excellence in emerging medtech like our AI-enabled imaging for structural heart, and $30 million to R&D adjacency in digital surgery platforms to compete with Johnson & Johnson's Ottava robotics. This positions us for sustained 100-200 basis point annual margin expansion, targeting 30%+ adjusted operating margins by 2026, even as ASP pressures from GPO negotiations persist.

Looking forward, we expect Q4 SG&A at 27.0-27.5% of revenue, with full-year guidance intact at 27.2-27.7%, incorporating $20 million in forex headwinds from a stronger USD. Risks include potential U.S. reimbursement tweaks under CMS's IPPS, but our scenario planning assumes no more than 50 bps dilution.

Moving on to competitive dynamics and market share trends.

Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining our Q3 earnings call for Apex MedTech. Before we dive deeper, I'd like to spend a few minutes on competitive dynamics and market share trends, as these have been top of mind given the intensifying landscape in medical devices. I'll break this down by key segments, regions, and our strategic positioning, with some forward-looking color on how we're navigating reimbursement headwinds, innovation cycles, and supply chain disruptions.

Starting with the big picture: the global medical devices market is tracking toward a $650 billion TAM by 2028, growing at a solid 5.2% CAGR, per our internal models aligned with Evaluate MedTech data. We're seeing tailwinds from aging demographics, procedure volume recovery post-COVID—now at 98% of 2019 levels globally—and the shift to value-based care, which favors our high-margin, minimally invasive platforms. However, competitive intensity remains fierce, with pricing pressures averaging 3-5% YoY in mature markets like the US and Europe, driven by group purchasing organizations and bundled payments.

In our core cardiovascular franchise—which drove 42% of Q3 revenue, up 16% YoY—we maintained our #2 position behind Edwards Lifesciences in TAVR, with structural heart market share holding steady at 18.2%, per our IQVIA tracking. We gained 150 basis points sequentially from Q2, capturing share from Medtronic's Evolut platform amid their supply constraints on low-profile sheaths. Procedure volumes for our ApexFlow TAVR valve grew 12% YoY to 28,000 cases globally, bolstered by our next-gen 14Fr system, which reduced vascular complication rates to under 1.5% in our pivotal RECOVER trial data—well ahead of the 2.5% category average. ASPs held firm at $32,500, a 1% increase, thanks to our evidence package supporting premium reimbursement under CMS's TAVR NTAP extension.

Orthopedics, our second pillar at 28% of revenue, saw more mixed dynamics. Knee and hip implant market share ticked up to 14.5% (from 13.8% a year ago), gaining ground on Stryker's Mako robotics ecosystem through our AI-enhanced ApexOrtho navigation suite, now in 450 US hospitals. Adoption here accelerated 25% QoQ, with case efficiency gains of 22 minutes per procedure, directly addressing surgeon feedback on Stryker's higher capex barriers ($1.2M per system vs. our $850K). That said, we're monitoring Zimmer Biomet's ROSA Shoulder launch closely; they chipped 80 bps from us in extremities, but our Q4 pipeline includes a cementless revision stem with 95% osseointegration at 12 months, per preclinicals.

Neurostimulation and neuromodulation rounded out at 22% of mix, where we expanded share to 22% in spinal cord stimulators, up from 19.5%, at the expense of Boston Scientific's WaveWriter Alpha amid their recall issues earlier this year. Our ApexPulse MR-conditional platform hit 15,000 implants YTD, with recharge-free designs driving a 4% ASP uplift to $28,000. Robotics is an emerging bright spot here—our collaboration with Intuitive Surgical on da Vinci-integrated neuromod leads positions us for 10-15% share in hybrid OR procedures by 2026.

Regionally, the Americas remain our fortress at 58% of revenue, with US market share across franchises at 16.8%, flat YoY but resilient amid UnitedHealth's Optum push for site-neutral pricing. Ex-US Americas grew 14% on strong Brazil and Mexico penetration via local manufacturing ramps. EMEA delivered 11% organic growth, share at 13.2%, fueled by NICE-in-the-UK approval for our TAVR valve and DGUV reimbursement wins in Germany—though NICE's proposed 10% tariff on high-cost devices looms as a 2025 headwind. APAC is the growth engine at 22% revenue mix, up 19% YoY, with China market share doubling to 8.5% in cardiology on our JV with MicroPort; we're countering local players like Peijia Medical's LeoValve with faster iteration cycles and a 20% cost edge via Singapore hub production. Japan and India contributed via PMDA-cleared robotics add-ons, offsetting regulatory delays.

Strategically, we're leaning into three imperatives to outpace competitors. First, R&D intensity at 12.5% of sales—above the 10.2% peer medtech average—funding 15 pipeline milestones this year, including our Zenith AI platform for real-time procedural analytics, which pilots showed 18% reduction in fluoroscopy time versus Siemens Healthineers' Artis systems. Second, M&A discipline: our $450M tuck-in of NeuroStim Dynamics bolsters SCS IP, targeting 200 bps share accretion by FY25. Third, supply chain fortification—we've derisked 85% of critical components (e.g., nitinol for TAVR) with dual-sourcing in the US and Vietnam, mitigating the 7% cost inflation peers like Abbott faced from China tariffs.

Looking forward, we expect modest share erosion in Q4 orthopedics from J&J's DePuy consolidation post-AbbVie spin, but offset by 5-7% procedure growth and our 300 bps gross margin expansion target. Consensus has us at 15.2% blended market share entering 2025, and we're on track to outperform via innovation moats and execution.

Next, procedure volume trends and market recovery commentary.

Turning to our procedure volume trends and market recovery dynamics, which continue to be the bedrock of our outperformance this quarter. In the Medical Devices sector, procedure volumes are the leading indicator of underlying demand, directly tied to patient acuity, physician adoption, reimbursement tailwinds, and procedural enablement from our innovation pipeline. We saw robust growth across our portfolio, reflecting a sustained market recovery now firmly in its expansion phase post-COVID headwinds.

Global procedure volumes grew 14% year-over-year in Q3, accelerating from 11% in Q2 and marking our seventh straight quarter of double-digit growth. This brought us to 108% of pre-pandemic 2019 levels on an adjusted basis, up from 102% last quarter. Organically, excluding FX and acquisitions, volumes expanded 12%, underscoring genuine market momentum rather than one-offs. This performance outpaced the broader industry consensus—think Boston Scientific's mid-teens cardiac rhythm management growth or Abbott's structural heart metrics—driven by our leadership in high-growth segments like structural heart, neuromodulation, and robotics-enabled surgery.

Breaking it down by franchise, our Cardiovascular segment led with 18% volume growth, fueled by a 25% surge in TAVR procedures. Our EvoFlow Pro platform captured 32% U.S. market share in TAVR, benefiting from expanded TAVR-to-5-year labeling from the FDA and strong data from trial extensions showing superior durability versus surgical AVR. In ablation therapies, pulsed-field ablation volumes jumped 40% YoY with our mapping system, gaining traction amid the shift from thermal RF ablation—similar to how Boston Scientific's FARAPULSE has disrupted the market. Coronary intervention volumes were up 12%, with drug-eluting stent mix shifting toward our next-gen platform, which now represents 45% of our stent ASP basket.

Orthopedics and Spine delivered 13% volume growth, reaching 110% of 2019 levels. Knee procedures grew 15% on the back of our Triathlon Total Knee System, with outpatient shift accelerating—now 55% of U.S. knees are ASC-based, up from 40% pre-COVID. Spinal fusion volumes rose 16%, propelled by our large-bore closure device enabling same-day hybrids. We're seeing healthy backlog conversion, with hospital OR utilization at 92% capacity versus 85% industry average per Definitive Healthcare data.

In our Neuroscience and Diabetes franchises, volumes expanded 11% and 16%, respectively. Deep brain stimulation for Parkinson's grew 20% with our neurostimulator, leveraging brain-computer interface sensing tech. Diabetes saw CGM sensor attachments up 22%, driven by our automated insulin delivery system, which now holds 28% share in the U.S. tubeless AID market, competing head-on with Tandem's t:slim X2.

Regionally, the U.S. remains our powerhouse, with volumes up 16% YoY—well ahead of the 12% consensus from ZS Associates' procedure tracking. Elective procedure rebound is complete here, with CMS reimbursement hikes for MS-DRGs supporting ASP stability at +2% quarter-over-quarter. Hospital systems like HCA and Tenet are ramping OR schedules aggressively, and we're benefiting from their focus on high-acuity cases.

Europe grew 9%, tempered by lingering inflationary pressures and NHI reimbursement scrutiny in Germany and France. Still, we're at 105% of 2019 levels, with U.K. NICE guidelines fast-tracking our robotic-assisted surgery system for soft-tissue robotics—volumes up 30% there. Structural heart procedures in the EU5 rose 22%, aided by our CE Mark for low-risk TAVR expansions.

Asia-Pacific was the star, up 22% YoY, led by China at 28% growth. Post-COVID elective recovery has been explosive, with National Reimbursement Drug List inclusion for our TAVR driving 50,000+ procedures annualized. We're also scaling our renal denervation system in Japan, where hypertension volumes grew 35% following PMDA approval. Emerging markets like India and Brazil contributed 15% growth, with affordable orthopedics kits enabling 20% penetration in tier-2 hospitals.

On market recovery dynamics: we're firmly past the trough. Global elective procedure suppression from 2020-2021 has inverted into a pent-up demand supercycle, amplified by aging demographics—global over-65 population up 3% YoY per UN data—and the shift to value-based care favoring durable devices. Supply chain snarls are behind us; our facilities are running at 98% utilization, with lead times down to 4 weeks from 12. Inflationary headwinds on raw materials eased to +1.5% QoQ, versus 5% last year.

Strategically, we're leaning into three tailwinds. First, procedural enablement via robotics and navigation: our robotic-assisted surgery platform hit 1,200 global installs, up 50% YoY, driving a 15% mix shift to robot-enabled procedures with 10-12% higher ASPs. This mirrors Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci dominance but with our multi-quadrant versatility.

Second, outpatient migration: 42% of our U.S. procedures are now ASC or office-based, up from 32% in 2021, boosting surgeon productivity and our attach rates for disposables—think 2.5x utilization on our systems.

Third, digital therapeutics integration: our AI-powered transcatheter valve analytics platform reduced procedure times by 18%, enabling 20% more cases per OR day. We're investing $250M in FY24 capex for AI/ML enhancements, targeting 5% volume uplift via predictive scheduling.

Looking forward, we guide Q4 volumes to 13-15% YoY growth, with full-year at 13%. Risks include potential Medicare sequestration cuts post-2024 election and Eurozone softness, but our 65% recurring revenue mix from disposables insulates us.

Then, strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter.

As we wrap up a solid Q3 where we delivered 14% year-over-year revenue growth to $2.85 billion—driven by strong U.S. core organic growth in our Cardiovascular franchise and Orthopedics—I'm pleased to outline our strategic priorities and focus areas for Q4. These priorities are laser-focused on accelerating revenue momentum, optimizing our cost structure amid ongoing supply chain headwinds, and positioning Apex MedTech for sustained double-digit growth in a market projected to expand at 5.2% CAGR through 2028, per Grand View Research.

Our overarching goal for the quarter is to achieve Q4 revenue aligned with our guidance, implying continued double-digit organic expansion. We'll drive this through five interconnected priorities, blending innovation, geographic expansion, operational resilience, commercial execution, and regulatory tailwinds.

Priority 1: Advancing Our Innovation Pipeline with High-Impact Launches (30% of R&D Allocation). Innovation remains our lifeblood in the Medical Devices space, where products with differentiated clinical outcomes—like our next-gen bioresorbable scaffolds—command premium pricing and market share. In Q4, we'll prioritize the U.S. commercial ramp of our EvoGuard TAVR valve, targeting full national rollout by quarter-end, with initial adoption projected at 150 U.S. sites, mirroring the trajectory of Abbott's Navitor platform.

Technically, we're accelerating AI integration across our portfolio: our PrecisionAI algorithm for real-time procedural guidance in Electrophysiology has cleared initial bench testing, showing 18% improvement in ablation success rates versus legacy systems. We'll file for FDA 510(k) clearance mid-quarter, investing an incremental $45 million in R&D—up 8% quarter-over-quarter—to hit three technical milestones, including 3D-printed custom orthopedic implants via our partnership with Stratasys. This positions us to capture 2-3 share points in the $15 billion global TAVR market, where procedure volumes are rebounding post-COVID.

Priority 2: Geographic Expansion, with Emphasis on APAC and Emerging Markets (Target: 20% Regional Revenue Mix Growth). U.S. remains our powerhouse at 58% of revenues, but we'll push for growth through expanded hospital contracts, including our GPO deal with Vizient. In APAC, which grew 22% in Q3, Q4 focus is NMPA approval for our NeuroStim DBS system—competing head-on with Medtronic's Percept PC—aiming for launch in 50 tier-1 hospitals. We're allocating $20 million to sales force expansion, targeting 18% revenue growth there, fueled by China's aging population and $10 billion neuromodulation opportunity. Europe faces MDR headwinds; we'll mitigate with selective launches. Emerging markets like India and LATAM get a $15 million boost for distributor buildout, eyeing 30% growth in value-based segments.

Priority 3: Operational Excellence and Supply Chain Resilience (EBITDA Margin Expansion to 28-30%). We'll target gross margin expansion through manufacturing optimization: ramping our Singapore facility to 85% capacity utilization for Electrophysiology leads, reducing lead times by 25% and outsourcing 15% of non-core components to diversified suppliers in Vietnam and Mexico.

We're also rolling out MedTech Lean 2.0, our digital twin platform for predictive maintenance, on track for $50 million annualized run-rate savings. This fortifies us against tariff risks, with 40% of our supply chain now reshored or nearshored.

Priority 4: Commercial Execution and Customer Engagement (Sales Force Productivity +12%). We're enhancing our field team with VR-enabled training on EvoGuard, projecting 12% uplift in rep productivity. We'll deepen hospital partnerships via our Outcomes360 data platform, sharing real-world evidence to support value-based care contracts—critical as CMS finalizes reimbursement rates with bumps for innovative devices. Expect growth in recurring revenues from our connected ecosystem.

Priority 5: Regulatory Momentum and Sustainability Integration. Q4 targets include IDE approval for robotic-assisted spine surgery and CE Mark under MDR for neuromodulation. We're budgeting $10 million for compliance, while embedding ESG priorities—reducing Scope 1 emissions 15% via electrified manufacturing—to appeal to investors and EU tenders.

Finally, revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter/year.

Good afternoon, everyone. As we wrap up a strong Q3 and look ahead, I'm excited to share our outlook for the fourth quarter ending December 31, 2024, and the full fiscal year 2025. Our guidance reflects continued momentum in our core structural heart and peripheral vascular franchises, bolstered by the successful U.S. launch of our next-gen EvoFlow TAVR valve and early adoption of our PulseSync robotic-assisted PCI platform. We've also navigated headwinds like persistent supply chain inflation in nitinol components and reimbursement headwinds in Europe, but our operational discipline positions us for accelerated growth.

For Q4 revenue guidance: We expect net sales of $1.25 billion to $1.28 billion, representing 7% to 9% reported growth and 8% to 10% organic growth year-over-year. This compares favorably to our Q3 results. Structural Heart remains our growth engine, projected at $650 million to $670 million, up 12% to 15% organically. The EvoFlow TAVR, with its lower-profile 14Fr delivery system and improved paravalvular leak rates below 2% in our pivotal GALILEO trial data, has captured mid-teens share in U.S. high-volume centers within three months of launch. We're on track for over 25,000 annual implants by year-end, outpacing competitors like Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien 3 Ultra. Internationally, CE Mark expansion into Japan via our partnership with Terumo should add $20 million in Q4.

Peripheral Vascular at $350 million to $360 million, flat to 2% organic growth, as we lap tough comps, but our new FlexiStent drug-eluting platform is gaining traction with 15% procedure share in U.S. outpatient cath labs. Capital Equipment, including PulseSync robotics, expected at $250 million to $270 million, up 10% to 14% organically. We've secured 12 new installs in Q3 across top-tier systems, with recurring revenue from disposables already at 35% attach rate, mirroring Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci model.

Regionally: U.S. (75% of sales): 9% to 11% organic growth, driven by Medicare Advantage expansion and Value-Based Care initiatives, improving case reimbursement by 3-5% through bundled payments. EMEA (15%): 5% to 7% growth, tempered by DRG pricing pressures in Germany but offset by 20% growth in the UK and Italy from TMVR clip adoption. APAC (10%): Flat to 3% growth, with China facing regulatory delays but Japan and India ramping.

On the margin front for Q4: Adjusted gross margin to 66% to 67%, up 100 basis points sequentially from Q3's 65.2%, thanks to a richer procedural mix and $15 million in procurement savings from dual-sourcing. Adjusted operating margin of 24.5% to 25.5%, expanding 150 bps YoY, as SG&A leverage outpaces R&D efficiencies. We're absorbing 2% FX headwind but mitigating via hedges covering 80% of exposures.

For full-year 2025 guidance, we're raising the bar with net sales of $5.3 billion to $5.45 billion, implying 10% to 13% reported growth and 11% to 14% organic growth—ahead of prior ranges and consensus. This assumes mid-teens structural heart expansion, fueled by full-year EvoFlow penetration to 30,000+ implants, PulseSync scaling to 50 new systems with $150 million in disposables, and a strategic tuck-in acquisition of a $200 million PAD portfolio, adding 1% to organic growth.

Adjusted gross margin for FY2025: 67% to 68.5%, up 200-250 bps from 2024's outlook, driven by scale in high-margin robotics (75%+ gross margins) and supply chain normalization—we've locked in 3-year contracts reducing cobalt-chrome costs by 10%. Operating margin expansion to 26% to 27%, supporting $1.4 billion in adjusted EPS at the midpoint (up 12%), with $800 million in free cash flow to fuel $2 billion in share repurchases and a TAVR pipeline including our bioresorbable valve in Phase II.

Key risks and opportunities: Upside from faster-than-expected FDA nod on our LAAO device (competing with Boston Scientific's Watchman), which could add $100 million. Downside from potential U.S. election-driven CMS cuts or renewed China tariffs. Strategically, we're doubling down on AI-enabled procedural navigation in PulseSync 2.0, partnering with NVIDIA for real-time imaging analytics, positioning us to capture 20% of the $15 billion robotics TAM by 2028 amid aging demographics and rising ASC volumes.

We're confident in delivering on these targets, underpinned by our 15% R&D-to-sales reinvestment and market-leading 95% on-time delivery.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah Chen for a review of our financial results.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, David. As David mentioned, we delivered a solid financial performance this quarter, with global revenue of $2.85 billion, 14% reported and 11% organic growth, adjusted EPS of $1.92 up 22%, and EBITDA margin expansion to 28.5%. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $3.2 billion in cash and equivalents, supporting our capital allocation priorities including the recent NeuroVasc acquisition and ongoing share repurchases of $500 million YTD. Free cash flow conversion was 105% of net income, reflecting working capital efficiencies.

For FY2024, we reaffirm our guidance of 11-13% organic growth and 28-29% EBITDA margins, with Q4 details as outlined by David.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Patel for an update on our product pipeline.

Dr. Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. We are making significant progress in our R&D efforts. Particularly excited about our ongoing clinical trials for HeartBridge, our fully implantable LVAD, which is showing promising results in advanced heart failure management, with interim data indicating 20% improvement in six-minute walk test distances versus current therapies. EvoFlow Pro continues to demonstrate superior hemodynamic performance in post-market surveillance, with paravalvular leak rates under 1%.

Our pipeline includes 12 late-stage programs, with $420 million invested this quarter. Key milestones ahead: Phase III readout for hypertension neuromodulation H2 2025, FDA submission for Zenith AI procedural analytics, and first-in-human for bioresorbable TAVR valves. We're also advancing VisionAI to full U.S. clearance, with 95% polyp detection sensitivity in endoscopy trials.

These innovations position us to address $50 billion in unmet needs across structural heart, orthopedics, and digital surgery.

Now, back to David for Q&A.

David Thompson:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: Press star then one. Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson - Goldman Sachs:
